questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No error’.**

If you had (1)/ told me earlier (2)/ I will help you. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__3__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The subordinate clause of the sentence: "If you had told me" is in the past perfect tense (subject + had + third form verb).To maintain the uniformity of the sentence the main clause will have the structure as "would have + past participle". Hence, the main clause will take the verb phrase as:- "would have helped".
 
• The given sentence is a third conditional sentence.
 
• A third conditional sentence is used to imagine a different past that did not happen.
 
• Some Examples:-

 If I had been present, I should have enjoyed it a lot. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dac933c583d88d7fbb203b5b7a234cec3fd685de718148e906afdace8b6dc680.png] 

 If I had been present, I would have enjoyed it a lot. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f6f8e13711bfe65ee7caffc30a728d21e8ef2dcdd208f14056c5bdc3aa26945.png] __

**Thus, the correct sentence is: ***If you had told me earlier I would have helped you.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No error’.**

Her mother is (1)/ angry and (2)/ indifferent to me. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2__**

**__*Key Points__**

 
• **'angry with' **should be used in place of **'angry'**
 
• If two **verbs/ adjectives **etc **take two different prepositions, we must mention both the prepositions, **we cannot simply use one preposition with the last verb/ adjective.
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• *She is **conscious of **and **engaged in **her work.*
 
• *I was **surprised at **as well as **pleased with **her performance.*
 
• She is younger and taller **than **her brother. (Single 'same' preposition is used with both the adjectives, it is used only one)*
 
 
 
• *​***Thus, the correct sentence is: ***Her mother is **angry with** and indifferent to me.*

questions.question:
In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.

Don’t loiter _____ the corridor. ** ​**
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: around 

**To ‘loiter around’ means to linger about aimlessly in a place.** ‘Loiter’ is followed by four prepositions, each having a slightly different meaning to it. ‘Loiter on’ means to move in a slow idle manner. ‘Loiter over’ means to waste time over work. ‘Loiter away’ means to waste time aimlessly.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

I will scold him when _____.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: he comes 

Solution: This sentence is an example of the first conditional sentence that talks about possible future events and their likely results. First conditional sentences follow the blueprint of a ‘conditional clause’ + the ‘main clause’ where the conditional clause is in simple present tense, while the main clause is in simple future. Thus, the sentence must be:** I will scold him when he comes.**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Dulcet**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Dulcet**.

• **Example:** She was frank about her concerns regarding the new policy.

• **Example:** Stealing is considered an immoral act.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. **

Dodge
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. "Avoid".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Dodge"** means to avoid something or someone by a sudden quick movement. (बचना)

 
 
• **Example: **He managed to dodge the question skillfully.
 
 
 
• **"Avoid"** means to keep away from or stop oneself from doing something. (बचाना)
 
 
• **Example: **She managed to avoid the busy traffic by taking a different route.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to **'Dodge'** is **'Avoid'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Avoid**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Soften** (मुलायम करना): To make or become less hard.

 
 
• **Example:** The butter will soften if left out of the fridge.
 
 
 
• **Order** (आदेश): An authoritative command or instruction.
 
 
• **Example: **The officer gave the order to advance.
 
 
 
• **Chaotic** (अराजक): In a state of complete confusion and disorder.
 
 
• **Example:** The city's traffic is always chaotic during rush hour.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Nebulous
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** Definite 

Solution: ‘Nebulous’ means ‘indistinct’ or ‘unclear’. Its antonym must be ‘definite’ which means ‘clear’.

 
• **Definite**: Clearly stated, decided, or fixed; not vague or uncertain. Something that is certain or conclusive, without any doubt.
 
• **Inchoate:** Just beginning or not fully formed; not fully developed or organized. Something that is in an early or incomplete stage.
 
• **Dismal:** Gloomy, depressing, or bleak; characterized by a lack of hope or optimism. Something that is dark, depressing, or miserable.
 
• **Sullen**: Silent, morose, or showing irritation or anger by refusing to speak or being sociable. Something that is sulky, gloomy, or resentful in attitude or appearance.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

P- The aim must be to ensure that our country does not experience either paucity or a-surfeit of trained manpower in any specific segment of our economy. 

<
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** QRSP 

The opening line must give us an insight into the paragraph. Sentence Q does exactly that and does not refer to any previously mentioned term or phrase. Thus, it must be the first sentence and that is Sentence Q.

R carries forward the idea of Q and refers to the nation’s growth which has already been mentioned in Q. Therefore, R must be the second sentence. 

Sentence S names the different sectors in reference to the phrase ‘different sectors of national growth’ used in sentence R. So, S logically forms the third sentence. 

The concluding sentence is P as it sums up the gist of the entire paragraph in a sentence.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

P- Bureaucratic cultures can smother those who want to respond to shifting conditions. </span&g
questions.solution:
**Correct Answer:** QSPR 

Solution: Sentence Q talks about how arrogant managers can evaluate themselves better than what they already are. This is what the entire paragraph rests upon and therefore must be the introductory sentence. Sentence S just carries forward the idea of Q by saying that these employees are not good at viewing the threats and opportunities. This must be the second sentence. P talks about the environmental situation faced by the organization due to the bureaucratic culture. P is the third sentence and is followed by R which comments on how the lack of leadership makes the organization crippled in such situations. It sums up the gist of the paragraph and is therefore the concluding sentence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

She teaches us English.

options.text: English is being taught to us by her.
We are taught English by her.
English have been taught to us by her.
We had been taught English by her.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer: **We are taught English by her. 

In the sentence ‘she teaches us English’, ‘she’ is the subject who is performing an action while ‘us’ is the object on which the action is being performed. Thus, in the passive form, the sentence must be 'We are taught English by her'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. **

Nisha said to Swati, " Will you help me in my project just now?"

options.text: Nisha told Swati whether she will help her in her project just now.
Nisha asked Swati if she would help her in her project just then.
Nisha questioned to Swati that will you help me in my project just now.
Nisha asked to Swati that will she help her in her work just now.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- __**Nisha asked Swati if she would help her in her project just then.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**​

 
• Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
 
• The tense of direct speech is changed only when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• When the direct speech is in an interrogative form, we follow the steps given below:
 
 
• The reporting verb said to is converted into asked.
 
• Connectors 'whether' or 'if' are used in place of comma and inverted commas.
 
• Change the reported speech from interrogative to assertive.
 
• The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
 
• ​Here the 2nd person 'you' will change into the 3rd person 'she' as per the object.
 
• Similarly 'my' is converted into 'her'.
 
• The auxiliary verb (will) in direct speech changes to (would).
 
• Words showing time and place are changed accordingly. (now- then)
 
 
 
• ​At last line up the remaining part.

 
 
• 
 
**Following these steps, we finally get-** *Nisha asked Swati if she would help her in her project just then.*
